subject: Durable furniture for daily commercial use
hook: 2 mm of edging is doing a lot of work on a reception desk
ig:
2 mm of edging is doing a lot of work on a reception desk.

Here's how we work on the front edges of commercial furniture. The leading edge of a desk, counter or staff kitchen unit takes constant contact: handbags, chair arms, trolleys, knees.

Thin edging on a busy front can chip or lift. So for high-traffic edges we use a thicker 2 mm ABS edge, applied on our edge bander, trimmed flush and finished with a slightly rounded profile. It's tougher against knocks and kinder on anyone brushing past.

Internal shelves and less exposed edges can take a thinner edge. Choosing the right one for each edge is part of the spec, not an afterthought.

If you're planning a reception desk or staff area, send us a DM and we'll talk you through edge choices.
fb:
Behind the scenes in our Hanley workshop: putting a proper edge on furniture that's going to get used hard.

For reception desks, counters and staff kitchen units, the front edge gets knocked all day. We use a thicker 2 mm ABS edge there, applied on the edge bander and trimmed with a slightly rounded profile, so it shrugs off bags and chair arms and feels softer to brush past. Less exposed edges get a thinner edge to suit.
